newsitem.title: NORWAY: Profit-taking hits Norway debt as crown stays weak.
newsitem.headline: Profit-taking hits Norway debt as crown stays weak.

text.p: Norwegian long bonds skidded lower as investors opted to take profit with the crown continuing to take a battering.
Dealers said February inflation figures and a government bond auction, both due on Monday, were adding uncertainty to the market.
The yield for the 2007 10-year bond jumped 12 basis points to 5.84 percent as the spread with German Bunds widened to 23 points.
The Norwegian currency fell to around 4.0970 against the mark during the session, before firming back to 4.0556 at 1541 GMT.

"The crown continues to come under pressure and short-term rates are rising. Bonds are down on profit-taking, it's a reaction to the long-term bull market," said one dealer. "Certainly the air is going out of the balloon."
He said he expected the spread with Bunds to widen further down to around 30 points.
"But I think it will be time to buy the crown again soon. I don't think we'll see it above 4.10 (versus the mark)," he said.
A Reuter poll of eight economists forecast Norway's consumer price index to rise by an average 0.15 percent month-on-month in February and 3.15 percent year-on-year.
